doc.title: Chico Hamilton interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 30, 2000

title: The power of the drum and his book
summary: Drums stop traffic and draw children; he names his book in progress.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Early drum kits and the gear drummers used

blocks.x: So see what I mean? And my instrument has been more devastating than bombs. You know to strike the fear into a human being. Hitler proved that when he had this march you know. In the early years of Africa the drums — hey you heard them, boom, boom, right? And the Indians — boom, boom, boom, boom you know? Hey man. As a matter of fact you could take, right here in New York, believe me, trust me, you could take a one hundred piece orchestra, or one hundred piece marching band, and let them march down Fifth Avenue, right? And people would say oh yeah, okay, that’s just the band, right? But you take one drummer, one man, or one kid with a drum and let him walk down Fifth Avenue playing it, and it will stop traffic. It will stop the world. Look at that, right? They don’t know whether he’s an idiot or what. And it will stop traffic. You take a kid to a music store, right? And just let him walk in the music store and the first thing he will do, he will go over to where the drums are and touch them. He won’t go to the trombones, he won’t go to the trumpets, he won’t go to the saxophones. It even outdoes guitars. He’ll go over to the drums.
It’s impossible for them to walk by it without—
Without hitting it or touching it.
It’s the skin you love to touch, which is the name of my book I’m writing. So anyway, I just wanted to get that in there.
